sourceQuestion.title: Explain horizontal partitioning, vertical decomposition, and sharding in a new case
sourceQuestion.context: Use the stated system behavior; call out assumptions that affect the conclusion.
sourceQuestion.prompt: A new implementation changes one constraint: A large PostgreSQL table is split by month on one server, while another system distributes tenant rows across several nodes. Explain which part of the original rule still applies and what must be checked before relying on it.
sourceQuestion.expectedAnswer: Horizontal partitioning divides rows into partitions of one logical relation; vertical decomposition separates columns and must preserve row identity for reconstruction. Sharding distributes data across separate nodes, while PostgreSQL declarative partitioning organizes partitions within one database cluster and is not by itself cross-node sharding. A complete answer explicitly connects this principle to the changed constraint and identifies any assumption that would alter the result.

sourceQuestion.title: Explain process isolation versus threads in a new case
sourceQuestion.context: Use the stated system behavior; call out assumptions that affect the conclusion.
sourceQuestion.prompt: A service keeps a large read-only model in memory and runs CPU-heavy jobs. Explain when a thread pool can share the model directly, what isolation a process pool provides, and what must be designed if separate processes also need shared data.
sourceQuestion.expectedAnswer: Threads in one process share an address space and can use the model directly, but a faulty thread can corrupt process memory. Separate processes normally isolate address spaces; sharing the model then needs an explicit mechanism such as read-only shared memory or loading a copy, with corresponding setup and memory costs.

canonicalPoint.conceptDescription: Choosing service, data, and communication boundaries.
knowledgePoints: Can justify a boundary using scale and failure reasoning.

sourceQuestion.title: Recall service boundary decisions
sourceQuestion.context: A component has a different scaling profile but participates in a latency-sensitive transaction with its caller.
sourceQuestion.prompt: Apply service boundary decisions to this case: A component has a different scaling profile but participates in a latency-sensitive transaction with its caller. What should the engineer expect, and why?
sourceQuestion.expectedAnswer: A boundary is justified when independent scaling, ownership, or failure isolation outweighs network, consistency, and operational costs; the boundary should follow a meaningful contract and data ownership. In the stated case, this means the design or diagnosis must account for the described constraint.
